messages:
Maya Patel: Quick question — the new slim-trace payloads from feature-x include a truncated customer_id in `trace.meta.cid` (first 8 chars). ACME asked for an immediate purge of their traces. Our config says request-logs TTL = 90d, traces = 365d. Is there an approved path for one-off deletes?
Sam Ortiz: You can do a targeted purge via the trace-pruner tool but needs SRE + Security signoff. Will need the cust id and the date range. Also note cache tombstones might keep fragments for ~7d after prune.
Maya Patel: Thanks. Cust id is acme-corp-42 (will DM full token). Range: 2025-11-01 -> 2026-02-20.
Jia Chen: @Maya Patel thanks — quick policy check: we only approve ad-hoc deletes for data subject requests or legal holds. For customers with contractual deletion clauses we can proceed. Can you attach the customer request or ticket?
Maya Patel: Filed ticket ENG-5432 and pasted their signed request there. Link: https://redwoodeng.atlassian.net/browse/ENG-5432
Eli Ramos: FYI pruning traces won't remove analytic aggregates (metrics) unless you request scrub of identifiers in those aggregates. Are we sure ACME wants everything gone?
Maya Patel: They asked for log/traces that include identifiers. I'll confirm re: aggregates.
security-bot: Policy snippet: "Ad-hoc log/trace deletion requires (1) customer-signed request or legal directive, (2) SRE execution, (3) security validation and change record." See https://docs.redwood/security/data-deletion
Sam Ortiz: Once we have the ticket and signed request, SRE can run the pruner. Steps: 1) Create infra-change PR referencing ENG-5432 2) Run prune in staging, verify 3) Run in prod with 1h maintenance window 4) Create audit entry.
ops-bot: Runbook excerpt:
```
# prune traces for customer
pruner --customer acme-corp-42 --start 2025-11-01 --end 2026-02-20 --dry-run
# verify results, then:
pruner --customer acme-corp-42 --start 2025-11-01 --end 2026-02-20 --execute --audit="ENG-5432"
```
Sam Ortiz: Note: prefix/KV caches may rehydrate old data for ~5m after prune if there's incoming requests; plan to throttle or put a short block.
Jia Chen: Security ok to proceed pending confirmation about aggregates and a signed deletion request attached to ENG-5432. Please cc me when you post the infra PR so I can sign off.
Maya Patel: Will attach the signed PDF and update the ticket. I'll also ask ACME if they want metrics scrubbed. Thanks all :pray: 
Eli Ramos: Also, if we need to delete entries from our cold S3 snapshots, that is a separate process (policy + ops lead). Ping me if that comes up.
Maya Patel: Good catch, will confirm and loop back.
Sam Ortiz: I'll pre-draft the infra PR template to speed the window once you confirm.
Maya Patel: Awesome — marking as blocking for release-2.1 until confirmed.
Jia Chen: Triage note: if customer requests are frequent we should automate a DMARC-style deletion flow. Logged as SEC-197.
Maya Patel: Filed SEC-197 follow-up. OK to close thread when ENG-5432 has attachments and PR created."
